note:
**The 1939 Register, ED letter code RMGC, schedules 2 to 144.** Nottingham registration sub-district 3, read from the page by A. Hagues. **Schedule 1 is Derby House and is already in the record**, so it is not repeated here.

**The register is shaped unlike a census.** There is no relationship column, so none is given; a household is held together by its schedule number, and the sub numbers give the order on the page. The birth dates are exact, which no census gives, and ages here are worked out to **29 September 1939**, the night the register was taken.

**Names written in capitals are later amendments.** A woman who married after 1939 had her new surname written over the old one, sometimes twice. Where the original is legible the record keeps it and names the amendment in the source line; where only the amendment can be read, that is said outright rather than guessed at.

## What this answers

**12 Cavendish Crescent North has its household.** Schedule 40: **Anne Rebecca Graham**, widow, born 2 July 1872, living on private means, with **John Leslie Graham**, company director, born 11 June 1896, and Mary Davies Andrew. This is the Graham family, and the house is no longer the record's blank.

**14 Cavendish Crescent North is still Fraser.** Schedule 41 is **Cecil Edward Fraser, solicitor, born 22 February 1884** - and the 1891 household the record holds at that house has *Cecil E R Fraser, son, aged 7*. The same man, the same house, forty-eight years on. It does not by itself settle where his father was enumerated in 1891, but it is a fourth strand in [[the-cavendish-road-east-ditto-run]], and the first one that is a date rather than a guess.

**Crescent Lodge is on Cavendish Crescent North.** Schedule 42. The 1891 page writes *1 Crescent Lodge* under the Cavendish Road East ditto marks. One of the two must be wrong, and it is the same ditto run that is already in doubt.

**Flixton is 15 Cavendish Crescent North**, confirmed again at schedule 47 - Robert S and Louise Lymbery, retired lace manufacturer.

**Noel Parker Woodward at 4 Western Terrace**, born 11 August 1882, works engineer. The 1891 round has him a scholar of 8 in his father Parker Woodward's household.

**Two on the notables list are here with exact dates.** **Richard Warwick Bond** at *Lynwood*, Tattershall Drive, born **30 September 1857** and entered as "Literary (retired professor)" - the record carries 1858. **Philip A Birkin** at 7 North Road, brewery director, born **24 September 1869** - the record carries 1870. Both are corrections the register makes outright.

**Ethel F and Dorothy Evans are at 6 Western Terrace**, both on private means, born 14 December 1864 and 13 February 1875 - the Evans sisters of the architect's family, still keeping house together at 74 and 64.

**Castle Rising, 3 Lenton Road** is kept by **Fanny Phoebe Cooper**, widow, born 2 September 1858. The record has Alfred James Cooper, retired lace manufacturer, there in 1921.

## What could not be filed

**Eighteen houses carry names the property list has not got**: *Lynwood*, *St Ives*, *Elmsdale* and *The Lodge* on Tattershall Drive; *Crescent Lodge* and *Pendower* on Cavendish Crescent North; *Cedar Lodge* and *Allendale* on Tunnel Road; *The Cottage*, *Brightlands* and *Engleholme* on Clumber Road East; *Brankston*, *Avalon*, *White Gates* and *Ravenswood* on Huntingdon Drive; and *The Lodge* and *Tower House* on Park Terrace. They are in the record unfiled, with the street as the page gives it. See [[house-names-live-in-prose]].

**Two named houses sit on the wrong street for the record.** The page puts **Sunnyside at 12 Park Valley** and the record has Sunnyside on **Park Terrace**; the page puts **Tower House on Park Terrace** and the record has Tower House at **53 Park Row**. Both are left unfiled. See [[named-houses-on-the-wrong-street-in-1939]].

**Standard Hill has no properties in the record at all** - not one of 1, 2, 3 or 7 Standard Hill, nor St Peter's Vicarage, nor the General Hospital Lodge. Five households, seventeen people, all unfiled.

**1, 2 and 3 Castle Grove are here and the record has none of them.** Schedules 95, 96 and 97 - Robert J Willatt the solicitor, George Lawson the estate agent and Charles William Shelton the valuer. The record's Castle Grove starts at 4. See [[castle-grove-has-no-low-numbers]].

**12 and 13 Park Valley are both occupied and neither exists in the record.** 13 is the Featherstone household at schedule 113; 12 is a nine-person guest house at schedule 121. 13 Park Valley was already wanted from 1881 and 1891, and 1939 makes it three rounds.

**Schedule 23 is written "8 Park Drive" and Park Drive has no number 8** in the record - it runs 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9 with Ashley House and Clumber House. This is the same trouble the 1891 round hit at "5 Park Drive". Left unfiled rather than moved on a guess.

**Schedule 50 is written "33" on a Cavendish Crescent North page** and the crescent has no 33. The word before it reads as Peveril. Unfiled.

**Schedule 24 is behind the closed band** and its address cannot be seen at all; four of its people are legible and are not entered, because a person with no house and no schedule address is not worth the risk of inventing one.

## Left out on purpose

**Brewhouse Yard is not in The Park** and the 1891 enumerator's own boundary says so in as many words - *"Lenton Boulevard (omitting Brewhouse Yard)"*. Schedules 52, 53 and 54 are at 8, 7 and 6 Brewhouse Yard and schedule 55 is the **Trip to Jerusalem**, where **George Ward**, born 13 April 1904, is victualler and brewer. Schedule 51 is **1 Castle Rock**, Samuel Roper Scales and Rose Mary Roper. None of the four is entered, because the record is the estate; the names are written here so they are not lost.

## What the later pages add

**Sir Albert Atkey is at 11 Park Valley**, schedule 112, entered as *Atkey Albert R (Sir)*, motor agent, born 1 July 1867, with **Lady Euphemia A Atkey**, born 13 January 1869. Two servants with them.

**Schedule 68 is Penrhyn House on Clumber Road East** - and it corrects a reading. The house had been taken for *Pendower House* from the previous sheet, where only the tail of the household showed; this page gives the address in full at the head of the column. Penrhyn *Cottage*, at schedule 59, is a different house on Cavendish Road East.

**Leslie F Bates, professor of physics**, at *Brankston* on Huntingdon Drive, born 7 March 1897.

## Fifteen empty houses

The register marks these as having nobody in them, and they are loaded into the unoccupied list so the gap tools stop offering them: **1, 2 and 3 Western Terrace**, **Gladstone House on Lincoln Circus**, **1 and 3 Duke William Mount**, **18 Cavendish Crescent North**, **Elmhurst on Cavendish Road East**, **3 Clare Valley**, **7 Huntingdon Drive**, **5 and 6 Castle Grove**, and **5, 21 and 2 Park Valley**. Six more are empty and are not in the record by name - *Castle Mount* and a house read as *Hoxmoor* on Cavendish Crescent North, one read as *Rosedale* on Cavendish Road East, the third of the four *Brightlands* on Clumber Road East, and *Avalon* and *White Gates* on Huntingdon Drive. One flat is empty inside an occupied house - No 4 of 1 Park Valley - so the house itself is not marked.
